turns.content: For three planets on circular orbits around the same star with the same Bond albedo of 0.3, derive the dependence of equilibrium temperature on orbital distance.
Combine that relation with Kepler's third law to express orbital period as a power of equilibrium temperature when the stellar mass dominates.
The temperature ratios are T1/T2=1.4 and T2/T3=2.3. Chain them to obtain T1/T3. The adjacent planet-mass ratios are 1.15 and 1.35; explain whether they enter the star-dominated period scaling.
Use the chained temperature ratio to calculate P3/P1.
How should this factor be qualified given the approximate temperature ratios and idealized radiative, orbital, and stellar assumptions?
Explain why the shared radiative assumptions and a dominant stellar mass matter to the scaling, and how departures from them would affect the inference.
Report P3/P1 together with the temperature-period scaling and its main qualification.
